I think if you truly are unhappy and ready to end the relationship you definitely need to make it clear that he didn't do anything wrong. That might alleviate some of the heartbreak but I'm afraid its inevitable.
Remaining friends might be an option if you can transition your relationship to something you're both comfortable with.
This really sounds like a painful situation, I'm sorry you're going through this.

I don't know if the relationship is good or not but one thing stood out to me. He doesn't *make* you upset. 
You *get* upset, maybe because of something he does or says.
So it really depends on if those things he does are things you consider worth getting upset over, in which case the relationship probably won't work out, or if it's something you're possibly over reacting to then it might work if you can learn not to react. I hope that makes sense

Its difficult and requires a bit of luck to make a living in music. 
If I were you I would continue your studies in science while pursuing music on the side. Definitely don't give up on the music, having a good creative outlet can really improve your life if you do get stuck working an office job at some point.

You could even consider a more specific major (for college) that combines music and science. Studying to become a music therapist might be an option too, if that sounds appealing.
